title: Weeknight trading to 9pm in metropolitan Perth (WA)
summary: The Retail Trading Hours Amendment Act 2010 let general retail shops in the Perth metropolitan area open until 9pm on weeknights, from 1 November 2010.

commenced.what: Act other than s 1 and 2: optional 9pm weeknight trading for general retail shops in metropolitan Perth (Gazette 22 Oct 2010 p 5207)

direction_rationale: Longer permitted trading hours let smaller and new retailers compete with incumbents on convenience and give consumers more choice; the PC recommended full deregulation. Effects may favour large chains able to staff extra hours.
comparison: States with unchanged trading hours (SA, QLD) and non-metro WA; Victoria/ACT/NT already deregulated
price_series: Food and non-alcoholic beverages (group); Garments for women; Garments for men
notes: Perth-only treatment: regional WA a within-state control if CABEE can be split by region (it is by SA2/LGA in some releases). Earlier in 2010-11, three Acts created special trading precincts with Sunday trading in Joondalup (from 8 Jul 2010), Armadale and Midland (from 23 Sep 2010), per the same history table. Evaluated 15 October 2026 (docs/results_wa_trading_hours.md, pre-registered): no detectable effect on general retail entry (+0.8 per 100, 90% interval -2.4 to +3.7) or exit (-0.1, -2.4 to +2.5) for this reform family; verdict inconclusive, grade Moderate. The direction field remains a hypothesis. Re-evaluated 18 October 2026 with new data, weeknight step alone (docs/results_wa_weeknight_2010.md, pre-registered): no detectable effect on the number of retail businesses in metropolitan Perth relative to regional WA (-1.8 log points, 90% interval -5.8 to +4.2) or on turnover of supermarkets, clothing and department stores (+2.0%, -4.4 to +7.2; not robust to the comparison); verdict inconclusive, grade Moderate.

verified.notes: Assent and commencement from the WA register history table (Gazette 22 Oct 2010 p 5207).

assessment.summary: Allowed general shops in metropolitan Perth to open until 9pm on weeknights. The Productivity Commission has recommended removing trading hours restrictions altogether.

marks.reason: Longer permitted hours let retailers compete on convenience and give shoppers more choice.

assessment.confidence_note: The archived econometric evaluation found no detectable effect on retail business entry or exit (grade Moderate).
